name: Rijksmuseum
description: The Netherlands’ national museum sits on Museumplein with masters from Rembrandt to Vermeer.

name: Anne Frank House
description: The canal-side hiding place where Anne Frank wrote her diary is now a museum with timed tickets.

name: Dom Tower
description: The Netherlands’ tallest church tower rises above Utrecht’s canals. Climbs give a view over the Dom square.

name: Kinderdijk windmills
description: A row of historic windmills stands on polder canals southeast of Rotterdam. Paths link visitor mills.

name: Het Loo Palace
description: A Dutch royal palace with formal gardens and museum interiors in Gelderland.

name: Jordaan canals
description: Narrow canals, cafés and courtyards make the Jordaan a favourite walking neighbourhood.

name: Keukenhof
description: Seasonal tulip gardens open each spring with vast flower displays near Schiphol.

name: Giethoorn
description: A village of canals and footbridges where boats replace most cars.

name: Markthal exterior
description: A horseshoe market hall with a mural ceiling anchors Rotterdam’s Laurenskwartier.

name: Zaanse Schans
description: A riverside open-air ensemble of windmills and wooden houses north of Amsterdam.

name: Albert Cuyp Market
description: Amsterdam’s busy street market sells stroopwafels, cheese and international snacks.

name: Markthal food stalls
description: Inside Rotterdam’s Markthal, stalls and restaurants serve under the arched apartments.

name: De Haagse Markt
description: One of the largest street markets in Europe sells produce and street food in The Hague.

name: Foodhallen Utrecht
description: A food-hall concept in Utrecht gathers casual kitchens under one roof.

name: Leiden market on the Rhine
description: Canal-side market stalls fill Leiden’s historic centre on market days.

name: King’s Day
description: Orange-clad flea markets and street parties fill Dutch cities each 27 April for Koningsdag.
